// the tour

The whole language, in programs that run.

Every sample below is a complete program or a slice of one, and almost all of them are copied verbatim from the compiler's example corpus, where each file is compiled and its output compared against a golden file on every test run. This page cannot quietly rot: when the language changes, these samples break the build until someone fixes them.

Hello, and the whole toolchain

A file is a complete program. No manifest, no project folder, no build file. fn run is where running starts.

examples/features/basics/hello.jet
// Your first program. `fn run` is where running starts.
fn run() {
    print("hello, world")
    return
}
$ jet run examples/features/basics/hello.jet
hello, world
$ jet run hello.jet # run it $ jet check hello.jet # check without running $ jet test hello.jet # run the #Test blocks $ jet fix hello.jet # apply the compiler's own fixes

Values

:: binds a value and it stays put. := binds a place you can reassign. Types mostly stay out of the way: they ride signatures and struct fields, and values carry them everywhere else.

run it
fn run() {
    name :: "Jet"
    year :: 2026
    print("values: {name} {year}")
    count := 0
    count += 3
    print("count: {count}")
}
$ jet run values.jet
values: Jet 2026
count: 3

Functions and effect rowsexamples/features/basics/signature_shape.jet

A result type sits bare after the parameters; -> starts the body. Effects split the arrow: -[IO]> says this function touches the outside world, and the compiler checks it. Omit the row and Jet infers it; write it and Jet enforces it.

examples/features/basics/signature_shape.jet
// D-SIG-SHAPE1=B: a result is bare after the parameters and `->` starts the body.
fn double(n: Int) Int -> n * 2

fn bump(n: Int) Int -[IO]> {
    print(n)
    n + 1
}

fn run() -[IO]> { print(bump(double(20))) }
$ jet run examples/features/basics/signature_shape.jet
40
41

Pattern matching is a tableexamples/features/basics/pattern_matching.jet

An arm table reads like the decision it makes. Or-patterns share a body, wildcards skip what does not matter, and else catches the rest.

examples/features/basics/pattern_matching.jet
fn describe_conn(c: Conn) String -> {
    if c == {
        .Active(id) | .Reconnecting(id) -> {
            // D-PATO: or-pattern — Active and Reconnecting share the same body.
            return "live:{id}"
        }
        .Idle(_) -> {
            // D-PATW: wildcard slot — Idle's payload doesn't matter here.
            return "idle"
        }
        .Closed -> return "closed"
        else -> return "unknown"
    }
}

Failure is in the signature

A function that can fail says so: Int !IOError returns a whole number or that error, and nothing else. Callers discharge the failure with ?? or let it propagate; ignoring it is a compile error. There are no exceptions and no error codes to forget.

run it
fn load_port() Int !IOError -> Ok(8080)

fn run() {
    port :: load_port() ?? 3000
    print("port {port}")
}
$ jet run failure.jet
port 8080

Defaults ride the typeexamples/features/basics/default_refs.jet

A default value lives on the parameter's type, and it may name an earlier parameter.

examples/features/basics/default_refs.jet
// D-NARG-D2 (S61): a default may reference an earlier parameter.
// `height: Int{width}` fills height with whatever width was given.
struct Rect {
    width: Int
    height: Int

    fn square(width: Int, height: Int{width}) Rect -> {width: width, height: height}
}

fn box_dims(w: Int, h: Int{w}, d: Int{h}) String -> "{w}x{h}x{d}"

fn run() {
    s :: Rect.square(5)
    print("{s.width}x{s.height}")
    r :: Rect.square(5, 3)
    print("{r.width}x{r.height}")
    print(box_dims(4))
    print(box_dims(4, 2))
    print(box_dims(4, 2, 1))
}
$ jet run examples/features/basics/default_refs.jet
5x5
5x3
4x4x4
4x2x2
4x2x1

Loops produce valuesexamples/features/basics/loop_values.jet

loop … in walks a collection. As an expression it collects results; add a guard to filter; break ends the prefix. One loop form, everywhere.

examples/features/basics/loop_values.jet
fn run() {
    values :: [Int]{1, 2, 3, 4}
    doubled :: loop value in values -> value * 2
    even :: loop value in values if value % 2 == 0 -> value
    prefix :: loop value in values -> {
        if value > 3 -> break
        value
    }
    nested :: loop left in [1, 2] -> loop right in [10, 20] -> left + right

    by_value := [Int:Int]{}
    loop value in values -> by_value.add(value, value * 10).drop("keys are unique")
    unique :: Set.from(loop value in [1, 2, 2, 3] -> value)
    lazy :: values.lazy().map(value -> value + 10)

Concurrency that cannot leakexamples/features/concurrency/tasks_join_all.jet

task spawns work and hands back a duty: every handle must be joined, raced, gathered, or detached on purpose. Forgetting one is a compile error.

examples/features/concurrency/tasks_join_all.jet
fn run() {
    // Join discharges the duty and yields the value.
    joined :: task work(5)
    print(joined.join() ?? panic("join failed"))

    // `all` consumes every handle in the list.
    results :: task.all {work(1), work(2), work(3)} ?? panic("task.all failed")
    print(results[0] + results[1] + results[2])

    task.group race_group {
        // `race` consumes both handles; the loser is cancelled.
        print(task.race {slow_one(), work(3)} ?? panic("race failed"))
    }

    task.group any_group {
        // `any` consumes both handles and takes the first success.
        print(task.any {slow_one(), work(4)} ?? panic("any failed"))
    }

    // `detach` discharges the duty for fire-and-forget work.
    background :: task work(6)
    background.detach()
    print("detached")
}

Files, honestlyexamples/features/io/files.jet

File operations return real errors and carry the FS effect. The happy path stays short; the failure path is visible.

examples/features/io/files.jet
use core.files as fs

fn run() {
    path :: "/tmp/jet_m10_files.txt"
    wrote :: fs.write(path, "hello\njet") ?? return Err("write failed")
    text :: fs.read(path) ?? return Err("read failed")
    print(text.to_upper())
    print(fs.exists(path))
}

The same language, in a browser

jet build --target web compiles a program to WebAssembly with a small JS bridge. The web backend is early and covers a checked subset. The marketing page's live counter is built exactly this way.

$ jet build --target web counter.jet # emits app.wasm, app.js, and a host page

The corpus these samples come from lives in examples/features in the repository, next to the golden outputs that keep them honest.
